text: In this paper, five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts, including a new highly efficient through-hole (TH) electroplating leveler, were synthesized from environmentally harmless coumarin compounds. The inhib itory properties of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were tested by electrochemical method, leading to the selection of the optimal leveler (C2). The adsorption capacity, adsorption state and adsorption sites of different coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts on copper surface were systematically analyzed, and the reasons for the different inhibition capacity of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts with different molecular structures were explained. The effect of C2 content on throwing power (TP) was studied, when C2 content was only 0.6 ppm, TP value was greater than 100 %. The adsorption behavior of C2 on copper cathode and the interaction between C2 and other additives were studied by the galvanostatic measurements (GMs). SEM and XRD tests were conducted to analyze the effects of different amounts of C2 on the copper plating surface.

text: With the continuous improvement of the modern electronic indus try’s requirements for electronic components, the demand for electronic components such as electronic chips that achieve miniaturization and high efficiency has also increased. The realization of high-density interconnection between printed circuit boards (PCBs) through micropore connection is an important means to realize the miniaturization of electronic products, so as to obtain more excellent electrical conductivity and space performance [1–3]. Acid copper electroplating is a key technology for copper interconnects in through-holes (THs), and it is also an indispensable technology in the manufacturing process of PCB. In order to obtain a flat and smooth plating layer and efficient TH filling, electroplating additives need to be added to the electroplating solution [4,5].

text: Electroplating additives are generally divided into inhibitors (generally polyethylene glycol and other polyether compounds, such as polyethylene glycol, polypropylene glycol [6,7]), accelerators (generally containing S–H bonds or S–S sulfonate compounds, such as sodium 3,3′-dithiodipropane sulfonate, bis-(sodium sulfoethyl)-disulfide [8,9]) and levelers (generally N-containing compounds, such as Janus Green B, diketopyrrolopyrrole [10–16]).

text: In the process of copper plating, through the interaction of different plating additives, the microhole can be overfilled. In the current research on electroplating additives, electroplating levelers have attracted much attention due to their irreplaceable properties. The leveler is mainly adsorbed on the surface of TH and inhibits the deposition of copper ions on the surface of TH, but has less inhibition on the deposition of copper ions inside TH, so as to achieve the effect of conductive copper interconnection or bottom-up copper electroplating [17–19]. The current research on levelers mainly includes the research of new leveler molecules (small molecule compounds [20–22], quaternary ammonium compounds [23–26] and macromolecular polymers [27,28]), interaction of different electroplating additives [29] and the effect of leveler concentration on filling efficiency and copper electroplating surface morphology [30]. Among them, quaternary ammonium salts have received more attention as leveler due to their superior leveling performance. For example, Myung JunKim [31] synthesized choline-based quaternary ammonium salt levelers and used them in TSV (Through Silicon Via) electrodeposition copper, Jinge Lv [32] designed and synthesized three water-soluble naphthalimide derivatives (NPI) and used them as levelers for microporous electrodeposition. Van Quy Dinh [33] used sulfonated diallyl dimethyl ammonium bromide copol ymer to fill the TSV bottom-up electrodeposition for 5 min to achieve no gaps. These studies have shown that quaternary ammonium compounds have good application prospects in the field of electroplating levelers, but it is still a difficult task to develop electroplating levelers with small additive amount, good leveling effect and environmental friendliness.

text: Herein, five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were synthesized by connecting coumarin-based compounds with pyridine-like compounds, including the first synthesis of large plane dicoumarinbased pyridinium quaternary ammonium salt C2 through a four-step reaction. The results of cyclic voltammetry (CV) test and polarization curve test show that C2 can be used as the preferred leveler. The band gap and electron cloud density distribution of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were obtained by quantum chemistry calculation and molecular dynamics simulation, in order to study the relationship between the molecular structure and inhibitory ability of these levelers. The experimental results of TH copper plating show that in a certain range, the content of C2 has a positive correlation with the TP value of TH electroplating, and can make the surface morphology of copper plating layer more smooth, and optimize the orientation of the crystal surface of copper particles. GMs results show that C2 can exert inhibition alone and has strong convection-dependent adsorption (CDA) behavior. C2 has competitive adsorption with SPS, no interaction with Cl -, and synergistic inhibition with PEG to form stable PEG-C2 complexes. This study expanded the application of coumarin derivatives and the design range of electroplating leveler molecules, hoping to provide some reference ideas for the development of more efficient levele molecules in the future.

text: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were implemented to calculate the adsorption capacity and the adsorption state of compounds A1 − C2 on copper from a theoretical level. Quantum chemistry calculations were based on DFT, the B3LYP function and def2-SVP basis set. The Gaussian 09 program was used to optimize the species geometry. Vibrational frequencies were calculated to evaluate the nature of the optimized structures at the same level. Next, the contour surfaces of the highest occupied molecular or bitals (HOMOs) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMOs) were visualized with Avogadro program. Electrostatic potential (ESP) surfaces were generated by Multiwfn and VMD software.

text: 4. Conclusion
text_index: 4. Conclusion
raw: 4. Conclusion

text: In summary, this study synthesized five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts and, for the first time, investigated their application as novel electroplating levelers in acid copper plating. Electrochemical measurements were used to analyze the copper plating inhibition ability of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts, leveler C2 with double coumarin structure had the strongest inhibition performance. Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation show that leveler C2 has the strongest adsorption capacity and the most adsorption sites on copper surface, which is the reason why C2 has the strongest inhibition ability. TH copper plating results show that the leveler C2 has good leveling performance, only need 0.6 ppm addition, can get 103.36 % through-hole TP value. The interaction between C2 and other additives and the mechanism of action were further explored by GMs test. The results of SEM and XRD show that the leveler C2 can make the surface of the copper plating layer smoother and optimize the orientation of the copper crystallographic plane. In this work, a new coumarin compound was synthesized for the first time and used as an electroplating leveler, which expanded the application range of coumarin compounds and the design field of molecular structure of electroplating leveler. It is hoped that it can be used as the basis for the development of efficient leveler molecules in the future.
